newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end lower, CRB slumps also.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end lower, CRB slumps also.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended lower again Thursday, with commodity funds seen probing the downside, leaving producers nervous, traders said.

"So gold closed around support at $378, a level seen briefly in early October, with the market looking like it wants to break down, but everytime it has done so lately, we've seen a bounce," Mitsui & Co USA bullion dealer, Greg Drury said.
The slump in the platinum/gold spread is resulting in some scale down buying in platinum and selling of gold in London," he said.
COMEX December gold ended down $2.20 at $379.10, after seeing a life-of-contract low at $377.70 intraday, with total estimated gold futures volume high at 60,000 lots.
In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted $377.50/378.00 an ounce, compared to the London Thursday afternoon fix at $379.50 and the New York close Wednesday at $380.15/380.55.
COMEX December silver settled down 2.0 cents at $4.808 an ounce, from an early low at $4.760, the lowest level for the December contract in two years.
In the bullion market, spot silver saw a low at $4.78 an ounce, the lowest level since March 1995.
"The silver market appears weak at the moment and could give way to longer term support at $4.72," CPM Group analyst Edward Kemp said.

U.S. economic news Thursday continued to provide no comfort to precious metals investors, with jobless claims in the week ended October 26 higher-than-expected at 342,000, sending U.S. bond yields lower.

On Wednesday the fall in U.S. third quarter GDP growth to 2.2 pct on annual basis, suggested the U.S. economy was slowing also, with little threat of inflation seen, and U.S. bond yields fell to nine month lows.

"With the bond market strong on evidence the U.S. economy is slowing, and inflation is no threat, there's little incentive for investors in precious metals or commodities in general right now," Smith Barney analyst Phil Tiger said.
NYMEX January platinum ended down $1.40 at $383.70 an ounce, not far from the life-of-contract lows seen Tuesday at $383.10.
The April platinum/April gold spread ended wider at $3.40 an ounce, recovering from a low of zero on October 25.
NYMEX December palladium closed down 75 cents at $116.75 an ounce, after seeing life-of-contract lows Tuesday.
The fall in precious metals, together with more losses in grain and energy markets, led to another sharp fall in the Knight Ridder Commodity Research Bureau (CRB) index.
Near the close of the Chicago markets, the CRB was down 3.75 points at 237.91, after seeing a session low at 237.78, its lowest level since October 1995.

"Its partly seasonal in the grains, but the weakness is broad across most commodities, as demand in the Far East is softening and it may take some time for commodity prices to build a base and recovery," Tiger said.
--Clive Mckeef, New York Commodities 212-859-1641; email: clive.mckeef@reuters.com
